new_findings.title: Portal apply health check has no checked-in implementation
new_findings.defect: The runbook requires installing /usr/local/bin/app-portal-health-check, but no implementation or installation procedure is present in the checkout. The deploy script requires APP_HEALTH_CMD to be executable before it can activate the portal.
new_findings.failure_scenario: An operator follows the runbook on a host without a separately provisioned helper and runs its --apply example; the deploy script rejects the missing health command, so the documented deployment cannot complete.
new_findings.fix: Add a versioned executable that checks both documented HTTPS endpoints and give the exact installation step, or identify a checked-in operator artifact and its installation source.

new_findings.title: Standalone drain GUC does not reach the documented schema heal
new_findings.defect: The runbook calls a standalone transaction-local set_config statement equivalent to ACX_BILLING_NAMESPACE_WRITERS_DRAINED=1, but sync_identity_schema opens its own database transaction. A GUC set in a separate SQL session is not visible to that heal; the migration only drops legacy global uniques when its own transaction GUC or the environment variable is set.
new_findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs the SQL snippet in one psql transaction and then invokes python -m scripts.sync_identity_schema in another connection without the environment variable. The heal can return successfully while leaving the legacy global uniques in place, so same IDs across billing namespaces remain rejected.
new_findings.fix: Remove the standalone SQL alternative or provide a supported schema-heal option that sets app.billing_namespace_writers_drained in the same transaction used by migration.heal, and show that exact invocation.

summary: The portal deploy contract suite passed; the runbooks have two medium integration gaps involving the missing portal health-check helper and a detached billing drain GUC.
